description:
Team Seven

Team Seven is a participant-led team interested in space exploration, scientific storytelling and the practical use of NASA's open resources.

For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we plan to develop Mission Echoes, a digital museum exploring the stories and scientific legacy of human-made equipment left on the Moon and Mars.

Our goal is to make space exploration history accessible through research, visual storytelling and an educational website. We welcome collaboration.
summary:
SPACE STAYERS is a digital storytelling museum developed by Team Seven for NASA's Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Inspired by the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten", the project explores the stories of human-made equipment left behind during space exploration, with a primary focus on the Moon and Mars.

Through a publicly accessible website, visitors can explore the Apollo Lunar Module, ALSEP, Lunokhod 1, Viking 1, Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner. An additional collection highlights historic deep-space explorers.

The project brings together mission histories, scientific achievements and historical context in an accessible digital experience. Its purpose is to preserve the legacy of space exploration hardware and encourage public interest in planetary science, engineering and space history.

SPACE STAYERS aims to make these forgotten explorers remembered by future generations.
details:
SPACE STAYERS is a digital storytelling museum created by Team Seven for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Inspired by the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten,” it documents the stories of human-made equipment left behind during space exploration, focusing primarily on the Moon and Mars.

Our public website presents selected missions and equipment, including Apollo Lunar Module descent stages, the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP), Lunokhod 1, Viking 1, Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner. A supplementary section also highlights historic deep-space missions such as Voyager 1, Voyager 2 and Pioneer 10.

The website organizes mission histories, scientific achievements and historical context into accessible stories. Visitors can explore the equipment, understand its purpose and discover why these objects remain significant.

We developed the website using Google Sites and created the project presentation using Canva. NASA mission-history pages and imagery were consulted for research and reference. AI assistance was used for research organization, language refinement and selected visual-design work, with its use disclosed in the project.

Our goal is to make space exploration history more accessible, preserve the legacy of these missions and encourage public interest in planetary science, engineering and exploration.
